verdict: All 16 acceptance criteria pass against the real files, and every load-bearing cross-file citation I could check was true rather than asserted. node --check passes on both. The production.data.js diff is purely additive against the pre-transport baseline (git diff 5811465 -- production.data.js shows zero deleted lines). auditCatalog() returns [] with freightdepot present; buildingCostAt(def,1) returns exactly the 35,000 cinder + 238 metal + 175 supplies + 125 stone + 75 fuel the comment claims, RUN not asserted; cost.js's dial constants are untouched; index.html is untouched. depot.js exports exactly the eight pinned names, contains no bare global (the single Profile hit is inside the globals-trap comment), no .from(/.rpc(/await/Date, and no second copy of the level ladder. Driving the module against the real catalog reproduced its own drift table to the digit (one L1 -> 4/4, two L1 -> 8/4, two L2 -> 16/8, three L3 -> 36/12) and its depots() measurement against the real routes.js exactly: flat and nested-only rows give identical inReach() on 1-hop and 3-hop, while a catalog radius of 1 on a level-2 row diverges false/true. Every depotReady() branch was exercised and each returns both a why and a fix; the catch answers in the same shape. The r4 correction is the right kind: the false claim was deleted rather than patched, replaced with a measured table and two consequences that survive measurement.
biggest_gap: depot.js is 916 lines carrying 228 lines of code — roughly a 3:1 comment ratio — and six of those comment blocks are 'AN EARLIER VERSION OF THIS COMMENT/PARAGRAPH/LINE/REVISION' corrections of the file's own unshipped drafts. This repo's convention reserves that chrome for incidents that reached players (60 rigs into a cap-4 charter; 270 units destroyed; 50,000 Cinder charged for a building that never persisted). Editorial history of a draft wearing the same red markers dilutes the signal, and a future reader now has to sort 'this was wrong in production' from 'this was wrong in a draft'. The concrete work: collapse the corrections into the single current statement of each fact, keeping only the one (the trg_ins/trigger mix-up) that names a mechanism a reader would otherwise re-derive wrongly from sql/038's header.

builder_response: Deleted the false claim rather than patching it. depots()' header no longer says a nested-only row resolves to `present: false` and is refused with "no depot" — it now says the opposite, marked as a 🔴 CORRECTED CLAIM, with the measured table showing flat and nested-only producing identical inReach()/quote() answers on both a 1-hop and a 3-hop route, and it names the failure as the same class fleetCap() corrects twice. The mirror is then justified on the two consequences that survive measurement: routes.js otherwise re-derives `3 + level` itself (a second author for the ladder — measured divergence: with a catalog radius of 1 on a level-2 row, a 3-hop haul is refused from the flat row and allowed from the nested-only one), and the resolved `bays` reads 0.
